chunks: And in it, Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfara'ini narrated from Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Fulan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever dies while knowing that he does not have an Imam from the Ahl al-Bayt, dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah).

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ: Ahl al-Bayt (the Family of the Prophet)
key_terms.مِيتَةً جَاهِلِيَّةً: Death of ignorance (pre-Islamic state of disbelief/ignorance)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of dying without recognizing the Imam in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to establish *al-Ma'rifah bi al-Imam* (recognition of the Imam) as the fundamental criterion for valid faith, distinguishing the era of the Prophet from the era of the Imams. By equating ignorance of the specific Imam with *Jahiliyyah*, the text underscores that Wilayah is not merely a political claim but the essential key to salvation, a concept central to Usuli and Akhbari debates regarding the necessity of knowing the Imam of the Age.
